text.short: Chino, 1940. A boarding house that still sets a boarders' table one Saturday a month.
text.today: Dinner comes in separate courses, not all at once. On the last Saturday of the month the house sets the Boarder's Table at 12:30 — one sitting, everyone together, the way the building fed men who worked the dairies.
text.history: It opened in 1940 as a boarding house for Basque immigrants.

x_kitchen.says: Basque, from the Pays Basque side of the Pyrenees

seating.note: Ordinary nights, your own table and separate courses. The last Saturday of the month, one long table at 12:30.

hours.text: Lunch Wed–Fri 11:30–2 · Dinner Tue 5–9, Wed–Sat 4–9, Sun 12–8 · Boarder's Table, last Saturday, 12:30
